title: Constant IO Locality and Pseudorandomness
summary: A broad counterexample does not settle the constant-locality setting; it remains open whether the resulting permutation is pseudorandom.

formal_statement.body: A main counterexample to the broadest version of the proposed implication does not refute the restricted setting in which each round permutation has constant input locality and constant output locality; in this setting, each input wire influences only a constant number of output wires, and each output wire is influenced by only a constant number of input wires. The open question is whether, for a randomized permutation $P$ satisfying these locality restrictions, negligible distance of its $T$-fold composition $P^T$ from 4-wise independence implies that $P^T$ is a pseudorandom permutation.

scope.domain: Mathematical foundations of mixing and pseudorandomness for randomized permutations with constant input and output locality.
assumptions: The round function P is a randomized permutation.
Each round has constant input locality and constant output locality.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether, under the constant input and output locality restrictions, negligible distance of P^T from 4-wise independence implies that P^T is a pseudorandom permutation.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source explicitly labels this statement Conjecture 5, a weakened variant not refuted by the paper's broad counterexample. It presents the implication from negligible distance of the composition from 4-wise independence to pseudorandomness as unresolved.
